summary: Valley County summit: a 1933 ground cabin (1934 in one source), first staffed 1935, destroyed in 1969; foundations seen in 2016.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1969. A 2016 ascent reported several foundations on the summit.

access.note: Hike-in site inside the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.

visit.trail_note: Class 1 route to the summit, per the climbing guide.

events.note: Ground cabin per firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the climbing guide; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1934
Forest Lookouts page: an R-1 lookout cabin was constructed; conflicts with 1933
Forest Lookouts page: first fire season the lookout was staffed
No cause given in these sources

evidence.quote: 1934: An R-1 lookout cabin was constructed.
1935: The first fire season the lookout was staffed.

evidence.supports: lookout within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness
evidence.quote: The lookout is within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.

evidence.supports: fire lookout placed on the summit in 1933
evidence.quote: A fire lookout was placed on the summit in 1933.
However, the lookout was destroyed in 1969.
There are several foundations located on the summit.
A 2016 ascent of the peak by John Platt and Dave Pahlas

evidence.supports: western edge of the Frank Church wilderness
evidence.quote: Chilcoot Peak is located on the western edge of the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.
This area is seldom visited by peakbaggers.

corrections.why: A 2016 ascent reported several foundations still on the summit; the ruins status describes footings remaining better than gone

notes_for_editor: Build year: 1933 in three sources (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, climbing guide) and 1934 for an R-1 cabin on the Forest Lookouts page, which also gives 1935 as the first staffed season; no source reconciles 1933 and 1934. The cause of the 1969 destruction is not given anywhere. Boise National Forest comes only from firelookout.com. Foundations rest on one 2016 climb report quoted by the climbing guide. The R-1 design is from the Forest Lookouts page alone; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say ground cabin. Access is public hike-in in wilderness per the sources; wilderness rules and current trail status were not checked for 2026.
